$comment: Structural spine. These are the grouping nodes that hold the per-subsystem fragments together, plus the navigation entries that guarantee the deep trunks (metals, petrochemicals, industry, peripherals) are reachable from the root even if no fragment references them by id.

roots.name: Mainboard ASSY 250407
roots.description: A single two-layer FR-4 board carrying the whole computer. Eight 4164 DRAMs make the 64 KB of main RAM; a 1 KB static RAM holds screen colour; the 6510 processor, the VIC-II, the SID, two CIAs, the PPI, a mask-programmed PLA and three mask ROMs do the rest, wired together with a dozen 74-series parts, three CMOS parts and a handful of small-signal transistors. Everything is through-hole DIP. About 320 components and 20 integrated circuits.
roots.note: Board ASSY 250407 is the long 'breadbin' layout, schematic 251138. Earlier revisions differ mainly in having no plated-through holes at all — where later boards have a via, the early ones carry a short single-core jumper wire soldered across the same pads. The U-numbers quoted throughout this tree are the canonical 250407 set and do not line up with the 250425, 250466 or short boards. A validated copy of the 250407 layout has zero vias and exactly two wire jumpers, E1 and E2.

roots.name: Rear and side I/O panel
roots.description: Everything you can plug into the machine. The back carries the 8-pin DIN video output, the 6-pin DIN serial (IEC) port, the 6-pin edge-connector datasette port, the user-port edge connector, the 7-pin DIN power input and the RF modulator's coax socket; the side carries two DE-9 control ports for joysticks and paddles; the bottom edge of the board exposes the 44-pin expansion socket. The video output is composite plus separate luma and chroma on an 8-pin DIN — which is one reason the RF modulator existed and one reason it did not need to be as good as it was.

roots.name: Where every branch terminates
roots.description: Everything above ends in one of three trunks: refined metals, petrochemicals, and the utilities and factories that supply both. Most component subtrees inline their own copy of the relevant chain — a capacitor really does carry its own aluminium, and an ABS case really does carry its own acrylonitrile — so these are the canonical, deepest versions of those same chains, kept together so you can read one end to end.

roots.name: Finishing and bundled extras
roots.description: Branches that hang off the machine rather than being part of it: how legends and colours were printed onto plastic, how one keyboard key becomes a bit, and the joystick that shipped in the box in some markets.

roots.name: Also required to use it
roots.description: A C64 shipped as a box with no screen, no way to save a program, and no way to enter one. In 1983 the machine was useless without a television set, a cassette recorder, and a joystick — arguably all three were part of 'a computer' in the way the question was meant.
